mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates elevated inflation, which typically leads to reduced real equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as central banks may accelerate tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with CPIAUCSL > 290, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 1.0% in a 3-month window, it signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises above 1.0% in 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to higher wage pressures and inflation, causing the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market expansion (HOUST above 1700 thousand units), the S&P 500 tends to rise as consumer confidence and spending increase, leading to positive forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months when HOUST > 1700, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 in a 1-month window signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as recession fears rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO falls below 105.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of real GDP (GDPC1) reflects robust economic growth, which typically supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in less than 45% of instances when GDPC1 is above the 2021 Q4 level (19731.119), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves rapidly.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 0.5% and RSAFS rises > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST rises > 0.5% and RSAFS rises > 0.3% in 1 month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% in a 1-month window, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE falls below 3.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
